audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer frames this as a range war Kassadin wins — tldr, winCon and phases[0] all tell him to 'win the lane at range' and 'own the range war' against a '125-range mana champ walking into your poke'.
audit.why: Ritual Nails is a 950-range projectile. Null Sphere is 650. Kassadin loses the poke exchange in every stage of the lane, and a player told to contest range will stand in nails for ten minutes.
audit.corrected: Reframed around the real difficulty shape: concede the poke war, farm to 6, and win on blinks. 950-versus-650 stated explicitly in tldr, early, phases[0], whys[1] and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was described as Purgatory 'rewriting fight math' and setting a 'floor', with no mention of what it actually does to Kassadin, and the two-items row claimed 'your takeover / your lane, full stop' while content win[6] and phases[6].side both read Skill.
audit.why: Locke's spike matters to Kassadin for a specific reason (see point 4) and the late-game overclaim contradicts the chart on the same page and a 50.82% win rate over 1039 games.
audit.corrected: phases[4] and phases[6] rewritten around grounding; spikes[2], content.late and whys[6] softened from 'your lane, full stop' to an edge that only exists outside Purgatory, matching the Skill rating the chart already carries.

audit.whatIsWrong: Purgatory grounds. Nothing in either layer says so, even though Riftwalk is Kassadin's only mobility and his entire post-6 plan.
audit.why: Purgatory carries the grounding property — it shuts off enemy dashes, and Riftwalk is one. A Kassadin inside the zone has no blink, which converts 'disengage above the floor' from advice into an impossibility. This is the single decisive interaction of the matchup and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Written into tldr, winCon, enemyWin, tradeBad, loading, phases[4], phases[6], content.mid, content.late, whys[4], whys[6], dontsFull[2] and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Silver Stake was described only as 'nail chip'. Its damage is magic on-hit and it is increased by the target's MISSING health.
audit.why: That changes the shape of every extended trade: the longer Kassadin stays low, the harder the passive hits — and because it is magic, Void Stone and the Null Sphere shield are genuinely on-type against it, which is why the lane is even at all.
audit.corrected: Stated in phases[3], content.early, content.late and wants.you[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization said 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.'
audit.why: Grievous Wounds reduces healing regardless of its source; a self-refund is still healing. The real timing rule is different: Soul Ignition pays its heal back at the END of the effect, so anti-heal only matters if it is already applied when the window closes.
audit.corrected: Reason replaced with the timing rule that actually governs it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block gave no numbers for anything and asserted Ashen Pursuit 'resets on takedowns'.
audit.why: Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s at every rank, Ritual Nails runs 10/9/8/7/6s at 950 range, and Purgatory is 120/100/80s. The takedown-reset claim is not in Riot's description of the ability and I could not verify it.
audit.corrected: All three real cooldowns written in; the unverified reset claim removed rather than restated.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late told the player to 'Q-silence the counterplay' in the shared Kassadin boilerplate.
audit.why: Null Sphere has no silence. Riot's text is damage, a channel interrupt, and a shield that absorbs magic damage.
audit.corrected: That sentence is not in this matchup's late block, but the same fabrication appears across the champion — flagged here and corrected wherever it appears in my slice.
